 Phillies Roster Moves after Tender Deadline
 In order to trade Orion Kerkering, they need to tender him. It’s fine.
 by Anthony Esbensen Nov 20, 2026, 11:04 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 The Phillies announced several roster moves with the deadline to tender arbitration eligible players expiring today.
 The Phillies avoided arbitration with Tanner Banks, Derek Hill, and Rafael Marchán. According to Jon Morosi, the Phillies agreed to a one-year, $1.3 million deal with Banks , who returns as left handed reliever depth.
 Brandon Marsh, Bryson Stott, Jhoan Duran, and Orion Kerkering were tendered, which means they could file to arbitration later in the off-season or agree to terms later. They’re not going to be free agents.
 Bryan De La Cruz, Moises Chace, Brett Harris, and Nolan Hoffmann were non-tendered, meaning they’ll each hit free agency and can sign with any club.
 De La Cruz comes as a slight surprise. He still carries a minor league option and became one of Don Mattingly’s most trusted options off the bench. He started in two of the three Wild Card games against the Atlanta Braves and hit .280 with a .762 OPS in 86 plate appearances during the regular season.
 Moises Chace is a tough story, he broke out after the Phillies acquired him and Seth Johnson from the Baltimore Orioles at the 2024 trade deadline. Chace showed a high-carry fastball with good velocity, a very good slider and a developing changeup as a starter. The Phillies protected him from the rule five draft in 2025 but he has been mostly sidelined the last two seasons because of Tommy John surgery.
 Brett Harris was a waiver claim earlier this off-season and Nolan Hoffmann was reliever depth.
 In another small trade, the Phillies acquired Jordan Leasure from the Chicago White Sox. Leasure already had Tommy John surgery in August and is set to miss the 2027 season to recover.
 To answer everyone’s question, it doesn’t seem like Tarik Skubal has signed with the New York Mets yet. Maybe later.
